title: Find a regression with bisect and worktrees
outcome: Use evidence to locate a bad change while keeping active work intact.
cue: Make the symptom repeatable, then search history.
version: Modern Git; check git --version for command availability

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A flaky network test points bisect at a random commit. Repair the investigation before trusting the result.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: You need to test the exact committed snapshot while your editor has unrelated changes. How can a worktree help?

trace.title: Known good and bad
trace.detail:
# The idea

Use history tools to answer a question, not to assign blame. log finds commits, show reads a patch, and blame points to the last change for a line.

That line may have moved during a refactor, so inspect context.

bisect narrows a regression between a known good and bad commit by testing intermediate commits. The test must be repeatable and its good/bad meaning clear.

A commit that cannot build may need to be skipped. A flaky test gives a misleading culprit.

A worktree is another checkout sharing the repository’s objects. It is useful for a review, a clean committed-snapshot test, or a hotfix while your current edits stay in place.

Each checkout still has its own working files and index. Respect branch checkout restrictions.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
For eight ordered candidate changes, binary search can often narrow the culprit with only a few checks. The exact sequence follows commit ancestry, not wall-clock guesses.

If the first bad commit is a dependency update, that identifies a trigger, not the whole root cause. Reproduce the behavior and explain why the change activates it.

Keep the regression test after the investigation.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail:
A bisect script with reversed exit meanings gives a confident wrong result.

Cleaning a worktree by deleting directories manually can leave registration behind; use git worktree remove for a clean managed checkout after saving needed files.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Use evidence to locate a bad change while keeping active work intact. Give a concrete failure example.
